title: Notary Public
body:
Notary Services

At Nooney & Dowdall LLP Solicitors, Shane Johnston provides comprehensive notary services for individuals, businesses, and organisations requiring authentication of documents for international use. As an experienced Notary Public, Shane is authorised to verify, witness, and certify a wide range of legal documents to ensure they are legally valid and recognised abroad.

Shane served his apprenticeship with Nooney & Dowdall LLP. In 1987, he was admitted to the Roll of Solicitors & started practising with the firm. In 1990, Shane became a Partner at Nooney & Dowdall LLP. Today, he is the Senior Partner. Shane also speaks fluent French.

His expertise covers a range of areas including Personal Injury Litigation, Medical Negligence Litigation, Commercial Litigation, and Employment Law.

Shane also specialises in Private Client work including Conveyancing Commercial, Conveyancing, Residential & Non Residential, and Wills, Probate & Administration of Estates.

What is a Notary Public?​

A Notary Public is a qualified legal professional appointed by the Chief Justice of Ireland to:

  • Authenticate documents for use outside of Ireland
  • Witness signatures
  • Certify true copies of original documents
  • Administer oaths and statutory declarations for international matters

Common Notary Services

  • Witnessing signatures on powers of attorney, affidavits, and statutory declarations

  • Certifying copies of passports, academic transcripts, and qualifications

  • Notarising documents for overseas property purchases or sales

  • Company documents for international business use

  • Documents required by foreign embassies or consulates

  • Adoption documents

  • Immigration and visa-related paperwork

Apostille & Legalisation

Some documents may require further certification by the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) in the form of an Apostille or Consular Legalisation. We can advise you on these requirements and assist in facilitating the process.

What to Bring

When attending your notary appointment, please bring:

  • Valid photo ID (passport or driving licence)

  • Proof of address (utility bill or bank statement within the last 3 months)

  • The unsigned documents you require notarised

  • Any instructions provided by the person or organisation requesting the notarisation
